summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, diabetes, migraines, and pseudotumor cerebri was admitted for recurrent severe headache and new-onset atypical chest pressure. Her blood pressure was severely elevated at 228/100 mmHg in the emergency department and responded to IV labetalol. Initial EKG showed non-specific ST-T changes, prompting concern for acute coronary syndrome, though serial troponins were negative. She had another episode of chest pressure that resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin. A nuclear stress test showed normal myocardial perfusion and left ventricular function, ruling out significant coronary artery disease. Her headaches persisted but improved with sumatriptan. Blood pressure was stabilized with the addition of lisinopril and adjustment of labetalol. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications, including aspirin for cardiovascular risk reduction, and expedited follow-up with pain management.
